message.content:
The campaign was not successful. Although the email channel had a higher overall average revenue per completed order (44.72 USD) than the paid_search channel (23.47 USD), this difference is due to confounding by customer segment. The email campaign was deliberately targeted at loyal customers, who have higher average revenue regardless of the channel.

When comparing within each customer segment, the email channel underperformed in every group:
- Loyal customers: email (82.44 USD) vs paid_search (108.09 USD), difference = -25.65 USD
- New customers: email (4.20 USD) vs paid_search (10.59 USD), difference = -6.38 USD
- Returning customers: email (26.80 USD) vs paid_search (34.70 USD), difference = -7.90 USD

The analysis excluded 809 completed orders after removing refunded orders and QA orders. The comparison within segments is valid because it controls for the imbalance in customer segment distribution (email has 131 loyal vs 26 in paid_search, and 64 new vs 304 in paid_search). The raw difference is confounded and does not reflect campaign effectiveness.

All evidence values were printed in the final code run and are directly traceable.
